tech.name: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI)
tech.status: Available in ChatGPT Work and Codex (Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Edu) and the OpenAI API
tech.one_line: OpenAI's new frontier model (Astra) and everyday model (Sol), priced per million tokens and sold on cost per task: Astra's input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra's, and on Agents' Last Exam, OpenAI says, it scored higher at less than a third of the cost, which OpenAI credits to better token efficiency plus a 20% discount on input and output tokens and a 60% discount on cached input; on FrontierCode 2.0, Sol came within 0.5 points of Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max). OpenAI's own results.

predecessor.name: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, picked by their price list (dollars per million tokens), assuming the cheaper rate means the cheaper job and the pricier model means better work.

claims.text: GPT‑6.2 Astra , our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol , our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. (row 1)
Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. (row 2, OpenAI's claim)

On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost (row 3; one test, OpenAI's result)

In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input ($8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output, all per million tokens). (row 5)
GPT‑6.2 Sol carries forward GPT‑6.1 Sol’s rates of $2 for input, $0.10 for cached input, and $10 for output per million tokens. (row 6)

GPT‑6.2 Astra costs significantly less per task than GPT‑6 Astra, driven by better token efficiency, a 20% discount on input and output tokens, and a deeper 60% discount on cached input tokens. (row 7)
GPT‑6.2 Astra leads the models we tested, up 6.2 percentage points from GPT‑6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens. (row 8, OpenAI's internal GDPval v2)
In Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, GPT‑6.2 Sol comes within 0.5 points of GPT‑6.2 Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max). (row 9)
FrontierCode 2.0 evaluates whether changes to real codebases meet maintainers’ standards for merging. (row 9b)
Tokens are the chunks of text models process and generate, so fewer tokens can mean a smaller bill even when the listed rates stay the same. (row 12)
Independent tests rank Astra second behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2, with no improvement in coding-agent performance. (row 13)
Those are company claims, not guarantees for every assignment. (row 15)
OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on Tuesday (article dated Nov 17, 2026; row 16)
Starting today, GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. (row 17)
